findings.title: The paper both asserts and disclaims that our 846-dimensional space equals Charton et al.'s B_21
findings.location: After Prop. prop:capfree, section-file lines 55-58 (paper/main.tex:931-933), against the paragraph 'Since \cite{Cha26} also report 846 coefficients' after Prop. prop:cha-ceiling, section-file lines 478-483 (paper/main.tex:1357-1358)
findings.quote: basis is the space $\mathcal B_{21}$ of \cite[Thm.~11.1]{Cha26}; its dimension,
findings.claim: Lines 55-58: 'Products of even power sums and even-part monomial symmetric polynomials span the same space, so our degree-21 basis is the space B_21 of [Cha26, Thm 11.1]'. Lines 481-483: 'We have not checked that their space is the same as ours (only the dimension is equal), so this is a located discrepancy ... not a refutation.'
findings.issue: These two statements contradict each other. The 'monomial symmetric' justification is left over from the old source note's misreading: notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md §(e), correction 4, records that Cha26's P_lambda is already a product of power sums P_j = sum x_i^j. On that reading B_21 = span{(L-P_1)^a P_lambda : lambda even, a+|lambda|<=21} is literally the family in our certificate, so the identity is direct and needs no spanning argument.
findings.analysis: The space identity matters for the Lemma 9.1 discussion. If it holds, Prop. prop:cha-ceiling (no P in V reaches 3.99 under Lemma 9.1's caps) together with Cha26's 4.00438 in B_21 shows that Cha26's value cannot come from the Lemma 9.1 caps. The paper's caveat at line 482 weakens this, but line 57 asserts the identity outright. A reader cannot tell which applies. I re-derived the dimension, sum_{n<=10} p(n)(22-2n) = 846, and our certificate's basis is (L-P_1)^a times products of even power sums, which matches the quoted definition of B_21 exactly. The only unverified points are Cha26's identification of 'repeated monomials' and the value of L in their (L-P_1), which the notes give as 53/50, the same as ours.
findings.evidence: notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md, section (e) 'Basis and dimension (§11, p. 42)' quote and 'Corrections' item 4; code/cert_ax45_capfree_D21e.json basis (846 entries, even parts only).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the spanning sentence at lines 55-57 by the direct statement that Cha26 §11 defines B_21 with products of even power sums (notes p. 42), so it is our family, with the same L=53/50 and dimension 846. Then either delete the caveat at line 482 or restrict it to the one remaining unchecked point (their identification of repeated monomials).

findings.title: Proposition prop:exact's region list (and capped_exact.py) silently uses g >= L - tau, which the statement does not assume
findings.location: Proposition prop:exact and proof of (3), section-file lines 151-152 and 194-197 (paper/main.tex:1026, 1069-1072); code/capped_exact.py Capped.tasks()
findings.quote: Assume $C_{m+1}\le C_m+g$ for all $m$ (this is Stadlmann's condition
findings.claim: Under C_{m+1}<=C_m+g alone, the corrections are integrals over the regions listed in the proof, including 'r_A >= C_{m+1}-(m+1)g and R>g (where U=g)' and 'the rectangle r_A<C_{m+1}-(m+1)g, rho<L-C_{m+1}-jg (where U=C_{m+1}-s)'.
findings.issue: Corr2 is an integral over admissible u' with |u'| <= tau (the J outer domain). The listed U=g and U=C_{m+1}-s regions impose only R>g, resp. U<R, which give |u'| < L-g. That is <= tau only if g >= L - tau. Without this hypothesis the proof's regions (and the code) include fibres with tau < |u'| < L-g that are not in J. capped_exact.py's Corr2b (Lam = L-(m+j+1)g) and Corr2c (rc = L-C_{m+1}-jg) tasks have no tau constraint and no assertion. capped_check.py does assert it ('need g >= L - tau'). Part (3) as stated, that the pieces are polygons, remains true in general, since adding |u'|<=tau keeps polygons, but the given proof and the implementation need the extra hypothesis.
findings.analysis: All parameter sets in the paper satisfy the hypothesis: Stadlmann 0.112 >= 0.06; Kintali 0.0728 >= 0.06; Charton (Table 3 and Lemma 9.1) 0.0656 >= 0.064, a narrow margin. So no number changes. The Kintali paragraph (line 504) shows the authors know the condition ('g >= L-tau, so our evaluators apply unchanged'). It is missing from Prop. prop:exact, from the Charton paragraph (lines 296-305) that lists the conditions checked for Table 3, and from capped_exact.py's own checks.
findings.evidence: capped_exact.py lines ~383-401 (Corr2b, Corr2c ranges without tau); capped_check.py line 159 'assert self.g >= self.delta'; arithmetic 41/625 = 0.0656 vs 53/50 - 249/250 = 0.064.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'and g >= L - tau' to the hypotheses of Prop. prop:exact (or add |u'|<=tau to the U=g and U=C_{m+1}-s regions in the proof). State that Charton's Table 3 and Lemma 9.1 parameters satisfy it (0.0656 >= 0.064). Add the same assertion to capped_exact.py.

findings.title: 'Lean-checked' counting facts are integer-unit analogues, not the real-coordinate statements used
findings.location: Proof of Prop. prop:exact, section-file lines 199-200 (paper/main.tex:1074-1075); Remark rem:ceiling line 283 (stadlmann_coord_le); Charton paragraph lines 304-305; lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean
findings.claim: The bounds m<=9, j<=3 (k=49), m<=16, j<=6 (k=45) and 'every coordinate of T is at most 0.6' are Lean-checked.
findings.issue: The Lean theorems are about lists of natural numbers in units of 1/1000 (Stadlmann) or 1/1250 (Charton), for example stadlmann_large_count: (l : List Nat) (h : forall x in l, 112 < x) (hs : l.sum <= 1042) : l.length <= 9. The paper applies them to real coordinates u_i > 0.112. The Nat statement does not formally imply the real one: flooring 1000u_i can give 112 and violate 112 < x, while ceiling can break the sum hypothesis. The real statements are true by the same one-line arithmetic (m g < sum <= L), so nothing mathematical fails. Only the evidence label claims more than Lean checked.
findings.analysis: This calibration matters because the abstract presents Lean-checked as the strongest evidence tier. The underlying facts are trivial, so the defect is only in the label.
findings.evidence: lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean: stadlmann_large_count, stadlmann_extra_le_three, stadlmann_coord_le, charton_large_count, charton_extra_le_six all quantify over List Nat.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restate the Lean lemmas over real (or rational) coordinates, or relabel these as 'Proved here (elementary; an integer-unit analogue is Lean-checked)' and say which units are used.

findings.title: Lemma 9.1 caps are smaller than Table 3 caps for every m >= 1, not only m >= 4
findings.location: Paragraph after the Lemma 9.1 display, section-file lines 342-343 (paper/main.tex:1217-1218)
findings.quote: of Table~3 for every $m\ge4$, so their support is smaller.
findings.claim: The caps of Lemma 9.1 are smaller than those of Table 3 for every m>=4, so their support is smaller.
findings.issue: Support inclusion needs the comparison for every m, and 'for every m>=4' does not give it. The comparison does hold for all m: C_1: 0.62 < 0.6216, C_2: 0.62 < 0.6352, C_3: 0.68 < 0.70, and C_m = 0.68 < 0.7336.. for m>=4. The conclusion is therefore right, but as written the premise is too weak to support it.
findings.analysis: Checked against the caps in code/cap6/P_ax45_D21_u.json and P_ax45_D21_u_lemma91caps.json (identical coefficient vectors, only the caps differ).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'for every m>=4' by 'for every m>=1 (strictly)'.

findings.title: The explanation 'the caps of Cha26 start lower' is wrong in every normalisation
findings.quote: the caps of \cite{Cha26} start lower ($C_1=0.6216$ against $L=1.06$) and
findings.claim: The caps cost more at k=45 than at k=49 because Cha26's caps start lower and g is smaller.
findings.issue: Cha26's first cap is higher than Stadlmann's on every scale: absolutely 0.6216 > 0.6, relative to L 0.5864 > 0.5758, relative to tau 0.624 > 0.611. The gap L - C_1 is also slightly smaller (0.4384 < 0.442), so the m=1 slab removed by the cap is relatively thinner. The caps for m>=3 are higher as well (0.70..0.8648 vs 0.68). Of the two reasons given, only 'g is smaller' (0.0656 vs 0.112) can explain the larger loss.
findings.analysis: This is explanatory text and no number depends on it. The measured costs (0.0095 vs 0.0041) and the corrections, which are dominated by Corr2c (the m=0 cut, 4.65e-3 vs 1.98e-3), are correct.
findings.evidence: C_1 values from cap6/P_capfree_D20_u.json (3/5) and cap6/P_ax45_D21_u.json (777/1250); L = 521/500 and 53/50.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete 'start lower (C_1=0.6216 against L=1.06)'. Keep 'g is smaller (0.0656 against 0.112), so more coordinates count as large', or give the measured breakdown (the m=0 cut Corr2c is 4.65e-3 of J against 1.98e-3) as the explanation.

findings.title: Stale forward-looking statements in the v0.6-0.7 text are contradicted by the v0.8-0.9 results in the same section
findings.location: Section-file line 255 (paper/main.tex:1130) and line 347 (paper/main.tex:1222); cf. Prop. prop:opt49 and Prop. prop:cha-ceiling (lines 405, 427)
findings.quote: would settle whether Lemma~9.1's caps can work at all (\lbl{Open}).
findings.claim: Line 255: 'optimising P on T itself (not done yet) can only raise the capped value'. Line 347: a test function optimised on the smaller support 'would settle whether Lemma 9.1's caps can work at all (Open)'.
findings.issue: In the same section, v0.8 optimises P on T (Prop. prop:opt49, 4.0124198) and v0.9 certifies that no P in the 846-dim space exceeds 3.99 under Lemma 9.1's caps (Prop. prop:cha-ceiling), with optimum 3.98555. Lines 255 and 347 therefore misstate the current status. Also, the reasons at lines 349-353 for not lowering the bound to 212 cite only 'with the other cap set our test function falls below 4', which is weaker than the later certified ceiling. What remains Open is only whether some F outside V works.
findings.analysis: This does not affect correctness. It affects calibration of the 212 discussion, which the brief asks about. The certification history in the context lines (v0.8: sigma=4 at 5000 bits; v0.9: sigma=4 and 3.99 at 6500 bits; runs/gram45_lemma91_recheck.log shows both 'positive definite ... True') is consistent with Prop. prop:cha-ceiling. Its residual dependence on capped_check.py alone at these caps is disclosed there.
findings.suggested_fix: At line 255 replace '(not done yet)' by '(done in version 0.8, Prop. prop:opt49)'. At line 347 change '(Open)' to a pointer: 'settled within our 846-dim space by Prop. prop:cha-ceiling (< 3.99); open only beyond it'.
